argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrow certification position, not a clean no-disclosure clearance. Aggregate readiness passes by 2.0 points and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, so launch readiness is supported at the overall system level. The same record also shows a 1.1-point miss in the multilingual customer-support segment, that the segment is named in two regional support commitments, and that legal has not closed the disclosure question. The defensible treatment is therefore certification with an explicit caveat that the no-disclosure position is not strongly supported on the current record.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for the requested treatment. The requested treatment is narrower: avoid escalation beyond what the admissible record supports by distinguishing overall launch readiness from the unresolved disclosure predicate.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not permit treating the 6% projected-traffic note as dispositive of immateriality, because the affected segment is tied to named commitments and legal review is still open. At the same time, the current audit concern appears broader than the admissible evidence requires if it is read as saying certification itself is unsupported. Operational-readiness evidence does support certification in a limited sense; what is not established by this record is full policy clearance for certification without disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. The correct policy reading is caveated compliance for certification, not a clean compliance finding for the no-disclosure position.
concessions: The multilingual customer-support segment misses target by 1.1 percentage points.
That segment is named in two regional support commitments, so the materiality question is real on the face of policy.
The release policy requires disclosure for material limitations in named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The legal disclosure ticket remains open, so the record does not support a strong no-disclosure conclusion.
